candidate.blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — use precautions to prevent injury and/or complications associated with a procedure or diagnosis; provide postoperative education
candidate.educational_objective: Use multimodal postoperative lung-expansion measures—deep breathing, coughing, early mobility and analgesia—with incentive spirometry as an adjunct.

options.A: Encourage deep breathing, directed coughing, early mobility, and adequate analgesia; use incentive spirometry as an adjunct.
options.B: Use incentive spirometry alone every hour and avoid ambulation until the client can perform the device without discomfort.
options.C: Keep the client on bed rest, limit coughing to protect the incision, and increase oxygen only if shortness of breath develops.
options.D: Restrict oral fluids and minimize position changes so incisional pain does not interfere with postoperative respiratory effort.

candidate.rationale: Postoperative pulmonary prevention is multimodal. The AARC guideline recommends incentive spirometry with deep breathing, directed coughing, early mobilization, and optimal analgesia rather than routine incentive spirometry alone. Bed rest, suppressing cough, and unnecessary immobility do not support lung expansion.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Postoperative lung-expansion prevention is multimodal: deep breathing, directed coughing, early mobilization and adequate analgesia; incentive spirometry is an adjunct rather than an effective stand-alone strategy.
